title: Quarterly evidence scrapbook: Q1 prep & micro-sprint notes
content:
Purpose and quick note:
This is a lightweight, intentionally messy "scrapbook" of signals I want to surface in my Q1 check-in and upcoming manager 1:1. Treat as draft evidence + micro-sprint timeline rather than a polished narrative. I will prune and pick 3–4 snippets to share in the meeting.

Top-line claim I want to land:
- Grew cross-functional onboarding quality for two platform teams while reducing escalations and saving ~12 engineer-hours/week of triage time. Result: fewer P1s and faster time-to-first-success for new hires on Dedicated onboarding flows.

Signal bank (raw snippets) — keep as-is, with metric or anecdote where possible:
- Onboarding triage pipeline: introduced a lightweight checklist + triage rubric that shaved mean incident reroute time from 48h -> 14h (sampled on 27 tickets). Context: many early issues were infra config + missing example prompts.
- New-hire setup docs: rewrote step-by-step GPU access doc; 4 people used it in Jan onboarding and reported "no blocker" on day 1 (vs previously 2 blockers per cohort).
- Cross-team playbook: ran two async office-hours (15–20 attendees) with engineers from infra, platform, and product. Follow-up survey (N=17): 82% said the session prevented an escalation or duplicated effort.
- Cost-savings prototype: brief experiment on batching/kv-cache default settings for non-prod that reduced token spend by ~8% in the sandbox (sample workload).
- Coaching: 1:1 with Tier-2 ops teammate to map escalation decision tree; they took ownership of 3 recurring tickets and closed them within the quarter.

Concrete examples I might read aloud (short):
1) "I rewrote the GPU access doc and paired with 3 new hires during their first day — they all finished hands-on setup without needing me. That freed up ~4 hours of my time that week and sped up their ramp."
2) "After the office-hours session, infra and platform agreed to a common label convention. That reduced cross-team misrouting — we measured a 30% drop in reroute tickets month-over-month."

Mini-evidence rubric (how I judge importance):
- Impact (time saved, incidents reduced, enablement breadth) — high weight
- Ownership (did I lead or enable someone else to own it?) — medium weight
- Durability (is this a one-off or a repeatable change?) — medium/high

Manager prep: phrasing & asks (short bullets to bring to 1:1)
- "Looking for feedback on prioritization: continue focusing on onboarding/tooling or shift toward formalizing rollout playbooks for Dedicated customers?"
- Ask: 1–2 headcount prioritization signals for next quarter (should I advocate for a .5 FTE on docs or coaching hours for on-call?)
- Calibration: "I think this work scales but need your read on whether this is promotion signal-worthy — I have impact, ownership, and a couple repeatable artifacts."
- Quick follow-ups: propose a short 30-min review with you to pick 3 artifacts to include in my promotion packet.

Risks and mitigations (short):
- Risk: Evidence looks operational-only (not strategic). Mitigation: Add an explicit strategic framing: how onboarding improvements unlock faster product iteration and reduce downstream support costs for customers.
- Risk: Metrics look noisy. Mitigation: surface sample sizes and the methodology (tickets sampled, cohort sizes).

Draft narrative (2–3 sentences for manager or Slack):
"This quarter I focused on reducing friction for platform onboarding and early incident triage. Small structural changes — a triage rubric, clearer GPU access steps, and cross-team office hours — cut mean reroute time and enabled teammates to own follow-ups; combined they free up ~12 engineer-hours/week and reduce duplicate work. Happy to walk through the artifacts and pick 3 for my packet."

Concrete next steps (commitments with dates):
- By 2026-03-12: extract top-3 artifacts into a single doc for manager review (triage rubric, GPU access doc, office-hours summary).
- By 2026-03-18: gather exact ticket counts and sample methodology to make metrics less noisy.
- By 2026-03-22: 30-min sync with manager to decide promotion-packet pieces.

Open questions I want to ask manager (short):
- Which signal matters more in your view: time-saved (engineer-hours) vs. number of teams enabled?
- Do we prefer a single long narrative or 3 concise artifacts for a promotion packet?

Quick TODOs (scratch):
- [ ] Add links to triage rubric + GPU doc (put in Confluence)
- [ ] Enumerate incidents helped by office-hours (ticket IDs)
- [ ] Pull sample-size data from Jira (Ravi help)
- [ ] Draft 2-line strategic framing for each artifact

Notes-to-self: keep this messy. When I turn it into the final packet, I will: 1) trim to 3 artifacts, 2) add concise metric lines, 3) ask for manager edits before I submit.

Random reflections — low stakes but useful to remember:
- Small enabling work compounds: the triage rubric felt boring to write but continues to prevent churn.
- Coaching is a force-multiplier: one handoff in Feb removed recurring ownership gap.

Appendix (links I will collect):
- GPU access doc (draft) — /confluence/people-ops/gpu-access-draft
- Office-hours notes (raw) — /confluence/people-ops/office-hours-jan-feb
- Triage rubric (spreadsheet export) — JIRA-2048

End.
